title: ₹59,000 crore is heading to Bihar — and that may not be the biggest story
summary: Capital is moving into Bihar with Adani Group planning ₹50,000–60,000 crore in infrastructure, Reliance Campa Cola investing ₹1,000 crore in Begusarai, and ₹51,600 crore in recent industrial MoUs.
content:
₹59,000 Crore Is Heading to Bihar — and That May Not Be the Biggest Story

Is Bihar entering a new economic cycle?

Something big is quietly changing in Bihar.

For years, one story dominated Bihar’s economy. People left. Bihar to Delhi. Bihar to Mumbai. Bihar to Bengaluru. Bihar to Pune. Young people often had to leave home to find better jobs.

Now, however, another story is taking shape. Capital is moving into Bihar.

Large companies are showing interest in the state. New factories are coming up. Big infrastructure projects are taking shape. Investment proposals are also growing.

The numbers are hard to ignore:

  • The Adani Group has announced plans to invest around ₹50,000–60,000 crore in Bihar over the next three to four years, covering power, roads, logistics, cement, and infrastructure.
  • Reliance Consumer Products, through its Campa Cola business, is investing around ₹1,000 crore in a bottling plant in Begusarai.
  • In August 2026, Bihar signed investment MoUs worth around ₹51,600 crore across sectors such as steel, textiles, food processing, pharmaceuticals, and nuclear energy.

These are separate announcements, not one single ₹59,000-crore investment package. Still, together, they point towards something much more interesting: businesses are starting to take Bihar seriously.

Why Are Businesses Looking at Bihar Now?

Large companies do not invest thousands of crores based only on sentiment. They look for markets, resources, and future growth. Bihar has all three.

First, the state has a huge population—a large potential consumer market with rising incomes and changing consumption patterns. Bihar also has a large workforce ready to support new factories, warehouses, and businesses. Moreover, improved roads and transport links make moving people and goods easier.

The state’s location between eastern and northern India allows businesses to reach multiple critical markets. Most importantly, Bihar still has enormous room to grow: instead of fighting for existing demand, businesses can help create new demand.

The Adani Investment Could Change the Conversation

The Adani Group’s investment plan stands out because of its size. The group has announced plans to invest ₹50,000–60,000 crore over the next three to four years across power, roads, logistics, gas distribution, cement, and infrastructure.

One major project involves a 2,400 MW thermal power plant at Pirpainti in Bhagalpur district. Better power supply helps factories operate reliably, and improved logistics reduces transit costs. Over time, these links create a wider business network for local suppliers, transport companies, and construction workers.

Campa Cola Brings Another Kind of Investment

Reliance Consumer Products plans to invest around ₹1,000 crore in a bottling plant in the BIADA area of Begusarai. Reports indicate capacity to produce around 200 million bottles annually and create more than 1,500 direct and indirect jobs.

This connects a major consumer brand with a growing local market, demonstrating that Bihar’s opportunity is not limited to heavy industry. Consumer businesses are entering as well, reinforcing the economic cycle.

₹51,600 Crore in MoUs Adds Another Signal

In August, Bihar signed MoUs worth around ₹51,600 crore across steel, nuclear energy, textiles, food processing, and pharmaceuticals. Notable proposals include:

  • Global Renewable Advanced Clean Energy: ₹22,500-crore nuclear energy project
  • Nakshatra Iron & Steel: ₹6,836 crore
  • Ankur Steel: ₹6,000 crore
  • Shri Langta Baba Metals & Power: ₹5,500 crore

While MoUs require approvals, funding, and land to become operational factories, the sheer scale signals that the conversation around Bihar has permanently shifted.

From Migration to Opportunity

For decades, migration shaped Bihar’s economic identity. Now, imagine a different situation: a young person finding a job near home, a local entrepreneur supplying a large factory, a farmer supplying a nearby food-processing unit, and a transport operator securing regular industrial contracts. That is the transformation capital can bring.

The Real Opportunity Is Bigger Than the Investment Number

It is easy to focus on headlines of ₹50,000 crore or ₹59,000 crore. But the bigger story is the direction of money: capital is looking east. When capital enters a region, it brings skills, technology, suppliers, and new business models, creating opportunities for people who previously had to leave.

title: Patna to Get High-Tech ₹21 Crore Indoor Stadium
summary: A state-of-the-art Indoor Stadium-2 is coming up at Patliputra Sports Complex in Patna with an investment of ₹21.20 crore, featuring multi-sport courts, 1,000+ spectator seating, and 40-bed athlete dormitories by March 2027.
content:
Patna to Get a High-Tech ₹21 Crore Indoor Stadium

Patna is getting a new indoor stadium. But the interesting part is not the ₹21.20 crore price tag. It is what Bihar plans to do with the facility after the ribbon-cutting.

A new Indoor Stadium-2 is coming up at the Patliputra Sports Complex in Kankarbagh, Patna. The project is estimated at ₹21.20 crore and is targeted for completion by March 2027.

The proposed facility will cover around 30,864 sq ft. Around 25,000 sq ft will make up the sports floor. It will also have seating for more than 1,000 spectators, athlete accommodation, broadcasting facilities, changing rooms, and warm-up areas.

On paper, it sounds like another sports infrastructure project. But Bihar’s recent sporting activity makes this announcement more interesting.

Patna Already Has a Sports Audience

Patliputra Sports Complex is not a new venue. The 16-acre complex has been operating since 2012. It already supports both indoor and outdoor sports. More importantly, the venue is being used.

The complex hosted the Bihar Women’s Kabaddi League in 2026. It has also hosted national-level competitions and international sporting events. In fact, Bihar’s sports calendar has expanded quickly. The state hosted the Khelo India Youth Games 2025 across five cities, featuring 27 medal sports, with Patliputra Sports Complex among the venues.

So, the new stadium is not being built into a sporting vacuum. There is already demand for competition space.

The Bigger Shift Is Happening Beyond the Stadium

Bihar’s sports infrastructure is increasingly being connected with talent development. The state’s Khelo India Youth Games impact assessment says upgraded venues are being positioned as dedicated training and high-performance centres for athletes with medal potential.

Meanwhile, the national sports policy environment is also changing. In 2026, the Union government announced the Khelo India Mission as part of a longer-term approach to talent development, coaching, sports science, competitions, and infrastructure. Then, in July 2026, the Union Cabinet approved a revamped Khelo India scheme and enhanced support for National Sports Federations with a combined outlay of ₹36,441 crore for 2026-27 to 2030-31.

That puts Bihar’s ₹21.20 crore project into a much larger national trend: India is investing more heavily in the sports pipeline, and Bihar is building more places for that pipeline to operate.

And This Stadium Is Designed for More Than One Sport

The proposed indoor facility will support several disciplines, including:

  • Kabaddi
  • Basketball
  • Boxing
  • Volleyball
  • Sepak Takraw
  • Wrestling
  • Gymnastics
  • Yoga

That flexibility matters. A single-purpose venue can remain unused between events. A multi-sport facility has more chances to stay active throughout the year. The planned retractable seating also allows the same sports floor to adapt between training sessions and larger competitions.

The Athlete Accommodation May Be the Most Important Part

The project includes separate 40-bed dormitories for male and female athletes. That means athletes can stay at the complex during training camps and competitions.

For a state like Bihar, this matters. Talent does not always come from Patna—it can come from a district, a small town, or a village. A talented athlete should not have to solve accommodation, training access, and competition logistics before they can even focus on sport. That is why athlete housing can be just as important as the court itself.

Bihar Is Also Getting More Comfortable Hosting Bigger Competitions

The Bihar State Sports Authority’s current calendar includes national and international competitions across multiple disciplines. Bihar hosted the Asia Hockey Cup 2025 for the first time, the ISTAF Sepaktakraw World Cup 2025 at Patliputra Sports Complex, and the Khelo India Youth Games in 2025.

Earlier, the challenge was: Can Bihar host major sporting events? Now another question is emerging: Can Bihar turn those events into a long-term advantage for its athletes?

A system where infrastructure, coaching, competitions, accommodation, sports science, and talent identification work together is where the real value of a new stadium could emerge when Indoor Stadium-2 opens its doors in 2027.

title: Prime Group to invest ₹1,500 crore in Bihar real estate, targeting 5 million sq ft Projects
summary: Prime Group plans to invest ₹1,500 crore in Bihar’s real estate sector over the next four quarters, developing nearly 5 million sq ft across residential and mixed-use projects.
content:
₹1,500 Crore, 5 Million Sq Ft: Why Prime Group Is Turning to Bihar

For years, Bihar’s real estate story was largely seen through the lens of Patna.

Now, something bigger may be taking shape.

Prime Group plans to invest around ₹1,500 crore in Bihar’s real estate sector over the next four quarters, with a development pipeline of nearly 5 million sq ft across residential and mixed-use projects.

The money matters. But the more interesting part is what this investment says about how the market is changing.

Prime Group Is Entering Bihar with a Large Development Pipeline

The group plans to use the proposed investment for residential and mixed-use developments across Bihar. This is not a single-project announcement. Prime Group is evaluating multiple development opportunities in the state and plans to expand its presence over the coming quarters.

The company has business associations across markets including Mumbai, Bengaluru, Kolkata, and Ranchi. It has now decided to bring that development experience into Bihar.

According to the company, it has also onboarded strategic investors from the Middle East, overseas architects, and specialist consultants for its upcoming projects. The details of these partnerships are expected to be announced later.

Why the 5 Million Sq Ft Figure Deserves Attention

₹1,500 crore is the headline number. However, 5 million sq ft tells us something different. It points towards the scale of development Prime Group is considering.

Residential projects will form part of the pipeline. Mixed-use developments will also be part of the plan.

That combination could matter for Bihar’s cities. A mixed-use development can bring housing, retail, and other commercial activity closer together. Done well, such projects can become small urban ecosystems rather than simply collections of buildings.

Of course, the final impact will depend on where these projects come up and how they are planned. That is where the story gets more interesting.

Bihar Still Has a Huge Urbanisation Gap

Bihar’s urbanisation rate remains far below the national level. The Bihar Economic Survey 2024-25 estimated the state’s urbanisation rate at 11.3%, compared with 31.2% for India.

At the same time, cities are growing. Patna’s urban population, for example, increased from around 16.84 lakh in 2011 to about 20.79 lakh in 2024, according to the survey.

This creates an unusual situation: Bihar has a relatively small urban population today, but its cities are gradually becoming more important centres for housing, education, healthcare, employment, and business. That creates room for organised real estate development.

The Opportunity Is Bigger Than Housing

When a large developer enters a market, the immediate conversation usually focuses on apartments and property prices. But real estate creates a much wider economic chain.

A large development can involve architects, engineers, contractors, construction workers, interior designers, building-material suppliers, security services, facility management companies, and local businesses.

Therefore, the effect of new projects can extend well beyond the project boundary. For Bihar’s entrepreneurs and smaller businesses, that supply chain could become an opportunity in itself.

Bigger Investment Does Not Automatically Mean Better Cities

There is another side to this story. Bihar needs more organised development, but it also needs better urban planning. More buildings alone won’t solve the challenges facing growing cities.

Road connectivity matters. So do drainage, water supply, public transport, parking, waste management, and open spaces.

That means the success of this ₹1,500 crore expansion should not be judged only by how many square feet gets constructed. The more important question may be: what kind of neighbourhoods will that investment create?

The Next Four Quarters Will Tell Us Much More

Prime Group has described the ₹1,500 crore investment as the beginning of its expansion in Bihar. That makes the next year particularly important.

We will eventually know where the projects are located, what they look like, who they are designed for, and how quickly they move from plans to construction. And that will tell us whether this is simply another large real estate announcement or the beginning of a broader shift in Bihar’s property market.

For a state with relatively low urbanisation but growing cities, the opportunity is clearly worth watching. The bigger question is whether developers can understand Bihar on its own terms instead of simply bringing a metro-city model into the state.

title: BharatNet to Bring Fiber Internet to Bihar Villages
summary: The revised BharatNet plan for Bihar aims to take high-speed fiber internet beyond panchayats directly into rural homes and institutions, targeting 99% uptime with modern ring topology.
content:
Bihar’s Villages Are Getting a Digital Lifeline: BharatNet Plans to Take Fiber Internet to Every Home

What if the next big change in a Bihar village does not arrive on a new highway, but through a fiber cable running quietly into homes?

That is the promise behind the revised BharatNet plan for Bihar, which aims to take high-speed internet beyond panchayat buildings and closer to ordinary rural households. The plan focuses on stronger village connectivity, direct fiber links for government institutions, and Fiber to the Home (FTTH) connections for families.

According to the report published on September 10, 2026, the Bihar government’s Information Technology Department has started work on necessary changes to its existing agreement with the Centre. The network expansion is expected to begin by the end of the year.

For Bihar’s villages, this could mean more than faster browsing. It could change how students study, how families access government services, and how rural institutions work every day.

What Is Changing with BharatNet in Bihar?

Until now, BharatNet connectivity in many villages has largely focused on reaching the gram panchayat level.

The revised approach aims to take that network further.

Under the plan, government institutions such as schools, police stations, anganwadi centres, post offices, health centres, cooperative institutions, and Krishi Vigyan Kendras will be connected through fiber.

More importantly, the government also plans to expand Fiber to the Home, or FTTH.

That means rural households could eventually get direct fiber internet instead of relying only on mobile networks or distant public connectivity points.

For a state with a large rural population, that distinction matters. A connection at a panchayat building is useful. A connection inside a student’s home, a village clinic, or a local business can be far more transformative.

Why Reliable Internet Matters in Rural Bihar

Fast internet is no longer simply an urban convenience.

A student preparing for an examination may need online classes, study material, or digital resources. A farmer may need access to online information and services. A family may need to complete a government-related process without travelling to a town.

Meanwhile, health centres and other public institutions increasingly depend on digital systems. Therefore, improving rural connectivity can reduce the distance between Bihar’s villages and the services available elsewhere.

The biggest opportunity may come from reliability, not just speed.

The 99% Network Uptime Target

The revised BharatNet model puts strong emphasis on keeping the network operational.

The plan targets around 99% network uptime. To support this, the network will use modern technology and a ring topology.

In simple terms, the network can provide an alternative route when one part develops a technical problem. As a result, a failure in one section should not necessarily bring the entire connection down.

That reliability could be especially important for institutions that depend on continuous connectivity. A village health centre, school, or government office cannot afford frequent interruptions when digital services become part of routine work.

From Schools to Health Centres: Who Could Benefit?

The proposed fiber expansion covers several parts of village life:

  • Students and Schools: Better internet could give rural students more consistent access to online learning resources, helping schools use digital teaching tools more effectively.
  • Rural Healthcare: Health centres with dependable connectivity can participate more effectively in digital health services and online processes, reducing unnecessary trips to larger towns.
  • Farmers and Rural Businesses: Small businesses, service providers, and local entrepreneurs increasingly need the internet for communication, payments, marketing, and online transactions.

What Could BharatNet Mean for Bihar’s Villages?

The larger story is about access. For years, the digital divide was often described as a gap between cities and villages. But that gap is not only about whether a person has internet access—it is also about the quality, reliability, and usefulness of that connection.

A young person in a Bihar village should not have to depend on an unstable connection simply because they live outside a major city. Similarly, a rural entrepreneur should have a fair chance to participate in the digital economy. That is why the shift from panchayat-level connectivity towards home-level fiber internet is significant.

Bihar’s Digital Future May Begin at Home

The real impact of BharatNet will not be measured only in kilometers of fiber laid. It will eventually be visible in everyday moments: a student attending an online class from home, a family completing an online service without travelling, a village entrepreneur speaking to a customer in another city, or a local institution staying connected when a nearby network route fails.

According to available details, the state has already started the process of making necessary changes to its existing arrangement with the Centre. The network expansion is expected to begin by the end of 2026.

When the internet finally reaches the last home in a village, the cable itself is only the beginning. What people build with that connection will tell the bigger story.

title: Bihar Gets ₹203 Crore Tourism Push for 3 Key Destinations
summary: From Bodh Gaya’s Buddhist Meditation Centre (₹165.44 Cr) to Sonepur Mela Ground (₹24.29 Cr) and Ambika Bhawani Temple (₹13.29 Cr), Bihar secures a ₹203 Crore tourism push to upgrade heritage and pilgrimage infrastructure.
content:
₹203 Crore Tourism Push for Bihar: Bodh Gaya, Sonepur Mela & Ambika Bhawani Temple Set for Development

Bihar has the stories. Now, three of its most important destinations are getting the infrastructure to help tell those stories to a much bigger audience.

From the spiritual heart of Bodh Gaya to the cultural energy of Sonepur Mela and the faith surrounding Ambika Bhawani Temple in Saran, three tourism projects are bringing a combined investment of about ₹203 crore into Bihar’s tourism infrastructure.

The projects cover three very different experiences — Buddhist heritage, cultural tourism and pilgrimage. More importantly, they could create opportunities for the people and businesses that depend on visitors.

According to government records, the Buddhist Meditation & Experience Centre in Bodh Gaya has received ₹165.44 crore. Meanwhile, tourist facilities at Sonepur Mela Ground have been sanctioned ₹24.29 crore. The Ambika Bhawani Temple project in Saran has received ₹13.29 crore under the PRASHAD Scheme.

Together, the three projects total ₹203.02 crore.

Bodh Gaya Gets the Biggest Tourism Investment

For a visitor, Bodh Gaya may look like a destination centred around its famous temples and monuments.

For millions of Buddhists, however, the place means something much deeper.

Bodh Gaya is associated with Gautama Buddha’s enlightenment. As a result, it remains one of the world’s most important Buddhist pilgrimage destinations.

That makes the ₹165.44-crore Buddhist Meditation & Experience Centre particularly significant.

The project comes under Swadesh Darshan 2.0, the tourism ministry’s destination-development programme. Importantly, the scheme places greater emphasis on creating complete tourism experiences rather than developing attractions in isolation.

Why the Bodh Gaya Project Matters

Better infrastructure can change how travellers experience a destination.

Instead of arriving, visiting one landmark and leaving, tourists may spend more time exploring the area. As a result, local hotels, restaurants, guides, transport operators and shops can all become part of the tourism economy.

Bodh Gaya also has something many destinations spend years trying to build: an established international identity.

Now, the opportunity is to turn that global recognition into longer stays, richer experiences and greater local economic activity.

Sonepur Mela Gets a ₹24.29 Crore Infrastructure Boost

Then there is Sonepur.

The Sonepur Mela is not a conventional tourist attraction. Rather, it is a living cultural experience that brings together traditions, commerce, faith, food and communities.

title: Gaya’s Vishnupad Corridor to Get a ₹2,520 Crore Makeover: Bihar’s 17 Big Development Plans Unveiled
summary: Bihar cabinet approves a ₹2,520 crore makeover for Gaya's Vishnupad Temple along the lines of Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, alongside ₹996 Cr Son-Falgu river linking and 15 other major development decisions.
content:
Bihar’s ₹2,520 Crore Vishnupad Corridor to New Air Routes: 17 Cabinet Decisions That Could Shape the State’s Future

From Gaya’s ancient pilgrimage traditions to better connectivity and water management, Bihar’s latest cabinet decisions bring several development priorities into focus.

Gaya could soon look different for millions of pilgrims. Smaller cities may move closer to improved air connectivity. Meanwhile, a proposed river-linking project aims to bring Son River water towards the Falgu.

These are among the key proposals in Bihar’s latest cabinet meeting, chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on September 15, 2026. The state cabinet approved 17 proposals covering tourism, water resources, infrastructure, aviation, and local businesses.

Gaya’s Vishnupad Corridor Gets ₹2,520 Crore Approval

For Gaya, the Vishnupad Temple is more than a religious destination. It is part of the city’s cultural identity and pilgrimage economy. The government has approved an administrative allocation of ₹2,520 crore to develop the Vishnupad temple area along the lines of the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor.

The proposed plan includes:

  • Temple complex development
  • Multilevel parking
  • Elevated pathways
  • Ghats and dormitories
  • Canteens and pedestrian bridges
  • Other modern public amenities

The Bihar State Road Development Corporation will implement the project, providing world-class infrastructure while enhancing opportunities for local hotels, shops, transport providers, and traders.

Son-Falgu River Project Receives ₹996 Crore Approval

The cabinet also approved ₹996.05 crore for the Son-Falgu river-linking project.

Under the plan, authorities will work to bring Son River water to the Falgu River through the North Koel Canal. The objective is to ensure year-round water availability in the Falgu River, which is sacred for pilgrims performing Pind Daan and critical for regional water management.

Bihar Approves New Water Resource Policy

The cabinet approved the Bihar Water Resources Restoration and Silt Management Policy, 2026.

The policy focuses on systematic desiltation of rivers, barrages, and reservoirs to restore their water-holding and water-carrying capacity. Extracted silt will be repurposed for road construction, railways, irrigation embankments, and flood protection structures, connecting ecological management with infrastructure growth.

Smaller Cities Could Get Better Air Connectivity

Bihar also plans to strengthen regional air connectivity through a new Memorandum of Understanding involving the Union Ministry of Civil Aviation, the Airports Authority of India, and the state government.

The proposal includes support for new air routes, viability gap funding for low-passenger routes during initial operations, and the development of heliports in aspirational districts to boost tourism, business travel, and emergency access.

Brick Kiln Businesses Get a Three-Month Relief Window

The cabinet approved a one-time settlement scheme for eligible outstanding dues of brick kiln operators up to the 2024–25 financial year, allowing qualifying debtors to clear principal amounts with interest waivers under notified conditions.

What Comes Next for Bihar?

These 17 cabinet decisions cover transformative areas that affect Bihar’s long-term economic trajectory—from pilgrimage infrastructure and river restoration to regional aviation and industry support.

title: They left Saran to build their careers, now they’re coming together to build Saran.
summary: A growing network of founders, professionals, and mentors is coming together through Saran Ventures to build a thriving local ecosystem for startups and innovation in Chapra, Saran.
content:
They Left Saran. Now They Are Coming Together to Build Saran.

For years, young people from Saran have left home for better education, jobs, and opportunities. They moved to Patna, Delhi, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Mumbai, and even abroad. Now, some of them are looking back.

A growing network of founders, entrepreneurs, professionals, mentors, and advisors is coming together through Saran Ventures to build something that Saran has long needed: a stronger local ecosystem for startups, entrepreneurship, and innovation.

From “Mahool Nahi Hai” to “Let’s Create It”

The idea began with Prabhat Kr. Singh, Founder & CEO of Digital Hashtag and Founder of Saran Ventures. Originally from Chapra, Saran, Prabhat noticed a familiar pattern among entrepreneurs and professionals from Bihar: many wanted to contribute to their home state, yet they often found limited local networks, mentorship, and opportunities.

In 2019, he began visiting Chapra and speaking with students, entrepreneurs, and professionals about startups and technology. That effort led to Jaago Saran, a community initiative focused on creating awareness around entrepreneurship and innovation.

The idea was simple: if people kept saying “Mahool nahi hai” (there is no ecosystem), then why not start building one?

From Conversations to a Growing Community

The initiative gradually moved from social media conversations to offline networking. One important gathering during Chhath Puja brought around 32 people from different backgrounds and sectors to discuss agritech, edtech, technology, services, and the challenges of building businesses in the region.

More importantly, the conversations highlighted a bigger issue. Saran had talent and ambition, but people lacked connections between founders, professionals, mentors, investors, and local businesses.

That thinking eventually led to Bihar Ventures Foundation, with Saran Ventures operating as an initiative focused on entrepreneurship, innovation, and ecosystem building.

Saran May Be Home, But the Network Is Everywhere

Not everyone connected to Saran Ventures lives in Saran today. Many founders and professionals work in cities such as Delhi NCR and Kolkata. Therefore, Saran Ventures has opened chapters in Delhi NCR and Kolkata, with a Bengaluru chapter also planned.

These chapters aim to connect people from Saran and Bihar who live outside the state and give them a way to contribute their experience, knowledge, and networks back home.

A Community Built by Many

Saran Ventures is not a one-person story. Its early contributors include:

  • Vijay Kumar: Founder of EduGaon and former founding member at Tata Digital
  • Avinash Kumar: Director at Work to Zone
  • Saurabh Nagvanshi: Director at Offerplant Technology
  • Vikash Singh: Director at Vxplore Technologies and Clinic Pay
  • Nilesh Dikshit: Founder of Just Go Fix

The initiative also has advisors with experience across technology, cybersecurity, government, and international business, bringing national and global experience into a community rooted in Saran.

What Has Saran Ventures Built So Far?

The ecosystem is still young, but it already has strong foundations in place:

  • 60+ members across startups, entrepreneurship, mentoring, investment, MSMEs, and IT
  • A network of 40+ IT professionals on LinkedIn
  • Connections with professionals in Luxembourg, Germany, and London
  • A plug-and-play facility with capacity for around 30 startups
  • One major startup meet and four to five networking meetups
  • More than 3,000 social media followers and 57,000+ impressions
  • Consulting support for startups in technology, marketing, and branding

What Could This Mean for Saran?

The real opportunity is not about turning Saran into another Bengaluru overnight. Instead, it is about making sure a young person with a business idea can find guidance. It is about helping local MSMEs understand technology and digital transformation, and connecting entrepreneurs with professionals and investors.

Most importantly, it creates a bridge for people who left Bihar but still want to contribute. Saran Ventures is now exploring partnerships around entrepreneurship training, private incubation, education, and social impact, with a broader five-year vision to build a self-sustaining entrepreneurial ecosystem.

They left Saran for opportunity. Now, they are bringing their experience, networks, and ideas back to help create opportunity at home. The bigger story is about what happens when a community decides to build its own “mahool.”

title: From Bihar to India: How Sudarshan Kashyap Is Building a Smarter Automotive Business
summary: From HouseBoon to BrooMax, Bihar entrepreneur Sudarshan Kashyap is building a technology-led B2B automotive commerce platform tackling everyday procurement challenges in India’s Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets.
content:
From Bihar to India: How Sudarshan Kashyap Is Building a Smarter Automotive Business

From HouseBoon to BrooMax, an entrepreneur from Bihar is tackling everyday procurement challenges in India’s Tier 2 and Tier 3 automotive markets.

The next big automotive business in India may not be built in a metro city. It may begin by understanding the problems faced by a retailer in a smaller town.

For Sudarshan Kashyap, entrepreneurship started with a simple belief: real business opportunities often hide in everyday problems.

Today, the Founder and CEO of BrooMax is building a technology-led B2B automotive commerce platform designed to make procurement more reliable for retailers across India’s emerging markets.

His journey, from co-founding HouseBoon to developing BrooMax, offers a closer look at what it takes to build a business outside India’s traditional startup centres.

From HouseBoon to BrooMax: Learning Through Experience

Sudarshan Kashyap’s entrepreneurial journey began with HouseBoon, a technology-led home-rental platform. The venture raised approximately ₹1 crore from angel investors and aimed to simplify renting through better trust and transparency.

That experience helped him understand product development, fundraising, and customer relationships. Later, after working in product management and technology, he returned to entrepreneurship with BrooMax.

However, his next business emerged from a different market. His understanding of Tier 2 and Tier 3 India helped him recognise challenges in the automotive aftermarket, where retailers often depend on fragmented supply networks and established supplier relationships.

Why BrooMax Is Focusing on Automotive Procurement

The automotive aftermarket connects manufacturers, distributors, retailers, and customers. Yet, procurement can become complicated when businesses manage multiple suppliers and face inconsistent product availability.

BrooMax aims to address these challenges through a B2B automotive commerce and procurement platform focusing on retailers in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Its objective goes beyond simply connecting buyers and suppliers—it seeks to improve access to products, supply reliability, and procurement efficiency.

“We don’t want to build just another B2B marketplace.”
— Sudarshan Kashyap

That approach reflects a practical understanding of the market. Technology can support a business, but retailers also need dependable supply and service.

When the Business Model Had to Change

Building in a relationship-driven industry brought its own lessons. BrooMax initially operated largely through an on-demand procurement model, allowing the business to enter the market with limited inventory.

However, as demand grew, the team recognised that connecting retailers with suppliers was not enough. Product availability and delivery speed also mattered.

“Availability and speed matter.”
— Sudarshan Kashyap

As a result, BrooMax began exploring inventory, supply density, and faster fulfilment. The experience reinforced a key lesson for Kashyap: entrepreneurs must know when to persist and when to adapt.

BrooMax’s Growth: Building from the Ground Up

According to reported company milestones, BrooMax has achieved:

  • ₹15–20 lakh+ Monthly GMV / sales
  • 100+ KL Total lubricant deliveries (with monthly volumes exceeding 10 kilolitres)
  • 500+ Buyers and suppliers served
  • 80%+ Reported customer retention

For Kashyap, crossing 100 kilolitres in lubricant deliveries represents more than a volume milestone. It reflects the retailer conversations, supplier relationships, and market learning behind the business.

Building from Bihar for the Wider Indian Market

One of the most interesting aspects of Kashyap’s journey is how he describes BrooMax’s identity:

“I don’t see BrooMax as a ‘Bihari startup.’ It is a startup from Bihar.”
— Sudarshan Kashyap

The distinction highlights his ambition to build a business with national relevance while retaining its roots in Bihar. BrooMax plans to expand across India’s emerging automotive markets. Its proposed dark-store approach aims to position inventory closer to retailers and improve fulfilment speed.

The company also envisions a technology-enabled procurement network connecting manufacturers, distributors, and automotive retailers.

A Message for Bihar’s Next Generation of Entrepreneurs

Kashyap’s advice to aspiring founders comes from his own experience:

“My biggest advice is simple: start with a problem you have actually seen. Build for the real India. Just Start. Because that’s the whole thing.”

He encourages young entrepreneurs to stay close to customers, use their local knowledge, and learn directly from the market. Smaller markets can present challenges, but they can also reveal opportunities that require local understanding.

title: Bihar to Sign MoU with Google India to Enhance Teachers’ AI Skills
summary: Bihar is bringing AI closer to the classroom. The state government is set to sign an MoU with Google India to train teachers across the state in AI tools, lesson planning, and digital learning.
content:
Bihar to Sign MoU with Google India to Enhance Teachers’ AI Skills

Bihar is bringing Artificial Intelligence closer to the classroom. The Bihar government is set to sign an MoU with Google India to improve the AI skills of teachers across the state.

The aim is to help teachers understand AI tools and use them in teaching and learning. The move comes as Bihar steps up its use of technology in education.

What is the MoU about?

Bihar will work with Google India to train teachers in Artificial Intelligence. The training will focus on improving teachers’ knowledge and practical understanding of AI.

The MoU will be signed by the Director of the State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT) and an authorised representative of Google India. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and Education Minister Mithilesh Tiwari will be present at the signing.

The partnership is expected to support Bihar’s efforts to improve technology-based learning in schools.

Why are AI skills important for teachers?

AI is becoming an important part of education and work. Therefore, teachers also need to understand how AI tools work. With the right training, teachers can learn how to use AI to support their daily work.

AI tools may help teachers prepare lessons, create learning material, and explain difficult topics. They can also help students learn in new ways.

However, AI will not replace the role of teachers. Teachers will still guide students, explain concepts, and understand their needs. The technology can support them, but the teacher remains at the centre of the classroom.

Bihar is also developing Bihar Vidya Saathi

The Google India partnership comes at a time when Bihar is exploring more AI-based solutions for education. The state is developing Bihar Vidya Saathi, an AI-enabled digital learning and doubt-solving platform aimed at helping students with learning and questions.

At the same time, Bihar is working with technology organisations including Google, Microsoft, and Sarvam AI. These efforts show that Bihar is looking at AI as part of its wider education strategy.

What could this mean for students?

The biggest benefit could reach students:

  • Teachers who understand AI can introduce students to the technology in a useful and responsible way.
  • Students can learn how to use AI as a learning tool and understand that AI does not always give the right answer.
  • Young people will enter a job market where AI is likely to play a growing role, and early exposure builds vital digital readiness.

For Bihar’s students, this could be an important digital skill for the future.

What does this mean for Bihar?

Bihar has a large network of schools and teachers. Therefore, teacher training can help take AI knowledge to a much wider group of students. The focus will also need to remain on access. Schools need suitable digital facilities for teachers and students to use new technology effectively.

Bihar has already started building this digital infrastructure in some schools. The state-level Teachers’ Day programme will also connect schools through live broadcasts.

Teachers’ Day programme in Patna

The state-level Teachers’ Day programme will take place at Shri Krishna Memorial Hall in Patna. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary will inaugurate the programme as the chief guest.

One teacher from each district will receive a state award for their contribution to education. The programme will also be broadcast live to schools across Bihar, including Kasturba Gandhi Residential Girls’ Schools, secondary, and higher secondary schools with smart classrooms and ICT labs.

The bigger goal is better digital learning

The Google India MoU is not only about teaching teachers how to use AI. It is also about preparing Bihar’s education system for new technology. The success of the programme will depend on how teachers use what they learn.

For example, a teacher could use an AI tool to prepare an explanation for a difficult topic. Another teacher could use it to create practice questions for students. The important thing is to use AI where it actually helps learning.

What happens next?

The MoU is an important first step. The next stage will be teacher training and implementation. Bihar will need to ensure that teachers across the state can benefit from the programme.

The change may start with technology. But the real impact will come from teachers using that technology to help their students. For Bihar, that could be the most important part of this new partnership.

title: Bihar Police to Set Up Child Help Desks in Every Police Station From October 2
summary: From October 2, 2026, Bihar Police will establish dedicated Child Help Desks in every police station statewide, providing child-friendly spaces, trained female CWPOs, and direct JJ Act protection.
content:
Bihar Police to Set Up Child Help Desks in Every Police Station From October 2: What This Means for Children and Families

A police station can be an intimidating place for any child. For a child who has experienced abuse, faced exploitation, or become involved in a legal case, that fear can be even harder to explain.

From October 2, 2026, Bihar plans to introduce dedicated Child Help Desks in every police station, creating a separate space where children can seek help or interact with police in a safer, more child-friendly environment.

The initiative, announced through directions from Bihar Police Headquarters, follows orders from the Supreme Court and provisions under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015. The objective is to make police stations more approachable for children who need care, protection, or legal intervention.

What Is a Child Help Desk?

A Child Help Desk is a designated area within a police station set up specifically for children. Instead of placing children in general holding areas or regular interrogation rooms, the help desk provides a separate, supportive environment.

According to the directives issued by the police headquarters:

  • Each desk will have a dedicated space, identifiable through clear signage.
  • The desks will be located in areas that make them easy to access, including suitable provisions for children with disabilities.
  • Essential facilities will include basic furniture, clean drinking water, age-appropriate toys, stationery, storybooks, and a child-friendly atmosphere.

The aim is to help reduce stress and anxiety when a child arrives at a police station.

Who Will Manage These Desks?

Each Child Help Desk will be managed by a designated Child Welfare Police Officer (CWPO), an officer not below the rank of Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI).

Where possible, authorities have directed that women police officers be assigned to the role. These officers will receive specialised training on child rights, child psychology, and relevant legislation, including the Juvenile Justice Act and the POCSO Act.

Why This Matters for Bihar

For many families, approaching the police can feel overwhelming, particularly when a child is involved. By creating designated help desks with trained personnel, the initiative aims to change that experience.

When a child in distress enters a police station, the first response often shapes how the case progresses. A child-friendly environment can help children feel secure enough to speak openly.

The real success of the initiative will depend on how effectively it is implemented across all districts. If supported with regular training and monitoring, these desks could represent a meaningful step towards making Bihar's justice system more compassionate and protective for children.
